We study the problem of sampling from the probability measure \mu(\mathrm{d}x)=Z^{-1}e^{-V(x)}\,\mathrm{d}x on \mathbb{R}^{d} , where V\in C^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d}) satisfies, for 0<\alpha\leq\beta , \alpha I\preceq\nabla^{2}V(x)\preceq\beta I\,,\hskip 20.00003ptx\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\,,\hskip 20.00003pt\kappa\coloneqq\tfrac{\beta}{\alpha}\,. (1.1) The main result of this paper is the following.

For every fixed y,\widetilde{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} and initial phase space point (x_{0},p_{0}) , the event-driven dynamics in Algorithm 1 , with the reference point fixed at \widetilde{x} , defines a unique non-explosive, time-homogeneous Markov process. The phase space measure \nu_{\eta,y} is stationary for this process. In particular, the returned position x_{\pi} is well-defined almost surely.
Fix y,\widetilde{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} . In the notation of ( 3.4 ), the bounce rate ( 3.9 ) reads
\lambda_{\widetilde{x}}(x,p)=\sqrt{\eta}\,[p^{\top}h_{\widetilde{x}}(x)]_{+}\,.

\displaystyle\Phi_{t}^{y,\widetilde{x}}(x,p) \displaystyle\coloneqq\bigl(c_{y,\widetilde{x}}+(x-c_{y,\widetilde{x}})\cos t+\sqrt{\eta}\,p\sin t,\;-\eta^{-1/2}(x-c_{y,\widetilde{x}})\sin t+p\cos t\bigr)\,,
\displaystyle\mathsf{S}_{\widetilde{x}}(x,p) \displaystyle\coloneqq(x,R_{h_{\widetilde{x}}(x)}p)\,,\hskip 20.00003ptR_{0}\coloneqq I\,.
The bounce map is an involution. Although there is a possible discontinuity at h_{\widetilde{x}}(x)=0 , this creates no ambiguity because the event rate vanishes there.
Let (E_{n})_{n\geq 1} be independent \operatorname{Exp}(1) random variables. Starting from \zeta_{0}\coloneqq(x_{0},p_{0}) at time T_{0}\coloneqq 0 , define recursively
\displaystyle S_{n+1} \displaystyle\coloneqq\inf\Bigl\{u\geq 0:\int_{0}^{u}\lambda_{\widetilde{x}}(\Phi_{s}^{y,\widetilde{x}}(\zeta_{T_{n}}))\,\mathrm{d}s\geq E_{n+1}\Bigr\}\,, (A.1)
\displaystyle T_{n+1} \displaystyle\coloneqq T_{n}+S_{n+1}\,,\hskip 20.00003pt\zeta_{T_{n+1}}\coloneqq\mathsf{S}_{\widetilde{x}}\bigl(\Phi_{S_{n+1}}^{y,\widetilde{x}}(\zeta_{T_{n}})\bigr)\,, (A.2)
when S_{n+1}<\infty . If the set is empty, set T_{n+1}=S_{n+1}=\infty and stop the recursion. Between jumps, set \zeta_{T_{n}+t}=\Phi_{t}^{y,\widetilde{x}}(\zeta_{T_{n}}) for 0\leq t<S_{n+1} .
To prove non-explosion, define the shifted harmonic energy
H_{y,\widetilde{x}}(x,p)\coloneqq\frac{1}{2}\,\bigl\{\eta^{-1}\,\|x-c_{y,\widetilde{x}}\|^{2}+\|p\|^{2}\bigr\}\,.
The flow and each bounce preserve this energy. Hence, with \mathcal{E}\coloneqq H_{y,\widetilde{x}}(x_{0},p_{0}) , every state produced by the recursion satisfies
\|p\|\leq\sqrt{2\mathcal{E}}\,,\hskip 20.00003pt\|x-c_{y,\widetilde{x}}\|\leq\sqrt{2\eta\mathcal{E}}\,.
Because \nabla V is \beta -Lipschitz, \lambda_{\widetilde{x}}(x,p)\leq\bar{\lambda}_{\mathcal{E}}(y,\widetilde{x}) throughout the path, where
\bar{\lambda}_{\mathcal{E}}(y,\widetilde{x})\coloneqq\sqrt{\eta}\,\beta\sqrt{2\mathcal{E}}\,\bigl\{\sqrt{2\eta\mathcal{E}}+\|c_{y,\widetilde{x}}-\widetilde{x}\|\bigr\}\,.
\int_{0}^{u}\lambda_{\widetilde{x}}(\Phi_{s}^{y,\widetilde{x}}(\zeta_{T_{n}}))\,\mathrm{d}s\leq\bar{\lambda}_{\mathcal{E}}(y,\widetilde{x})\,u\,.
If \bar{\lambda}_{\mathcal{E}}(y,\widetilde{x})=0 , the event rate vanishes and there are no jumps. Otherwise, ( A.1 ) implies, for every finite waiting time,
S_{n+1}\geq\frac{E_{n+1}}{\bar{\lambda}_{\mathcal{E}}(y,\widetilde{x})}\,.
T_{n}\geq\frac{\sum_{j=1}^{n}E_{j}}{\bar{\lambda}_{\mathcal{E}}(y,\widetilde{x})}\longrightarrow\infty

Finally, the memoryless property of the exponential clocks gives the time-homogeneous Markov property. This is precisely the integrated hazard construction of Davis [ 12 , Section 2] . ∎

The pathwise argument below proves the same identity without requiring differentiability or continuity of the bounce map.

Invariance and Jensen’s inequality give \|\mathsf{T}_{t}^{y,\widetilde{x}}F\|_{2}\leq\|F\|_{2} . It remains to prove strong continuity. For F\in C_{\rm c}(\mathbb{R}^{2d}) , the deterministic flow converges to the identity as t\searrow 0 , and the probability of a jump before time t is
1-\exp\Bigl\{-\int_{0}^{t}\lambda_{\widetilde{x}}(\Phi_{s}^{y,\widetilde{x}}\zeta)\,\mathrm{d}s\Bigr\}\longrightarrow 0\,.
Dominated convergence therefore gives \mathsf{T}_{t}^{y,\widetilde{x}}F\to F in L^{2} . Density of C_{\rm c}(\mathbb{R}^{2d}) and contractivity extend this to all F\in L^{2} .

Since \nabla V is continuous, the harmonic flow, event rate, and reflection map are jointly Borel; the convention R_{0}=I ensures this even where the reflection normal vanishes. The integrated hazard is jointly Borel, with continuous, nondecreasing dependence on time, so its threshold-crossing times are Borel, as can be checked using rational times. Thus the recursion ( A.1 )–( A.2 ) makes each jump time and post-jump state Borel in (y,x_{0},p_{0},\widetilde{x},(E_{j})_{j\geq 1}) . By non-explosion, the terminal state at time \pi is the almost-sure limit of the Borel terminal states obtained by allowing at most n jumps. Setting the limit to zero wherever it does not exist gives a Borel version.

The conditional density in ( 2.8 ) is jointly Borel in (y,\widetilde{x}) . Integrating \mathbf{1}_{\{x_{\pi}\in A\}} against this reference law and the laws of the Gaussian momentum and exponential clocks therefore makes (y,x)\mapsto\mathcal{H}_{y}(x,A) Borel for every Borel set A .
